newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat harvest accelerates amid high winds.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat harvest accelerates amid high winds.

text.p: High winds helped dry wheat fields and accelerated harvesting in Oklahoma during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
"Yields were better than what was anticipated a month ago, topping 60 bushels per acre in areas of north central Oklahoma. However, some blank heads have also been reported," the report said.
Statewide, the wheat crop was 40 percent harvested, lagging the 84 percent pace of last year and 59 percent for the five-year average.

The state's wheat improved and was rated two percent very poor, nine poor, 27 fair, 58 good and four percent excellent. A week ago, the crop was rated seven percent very poor, 10 poor, 28 fair, 52 good and three percent excellent.
Soybeans were 76 percent planted, against 68 last week, 93 last year and 68 percent on average.
Sorghum acreage was 84 percent planted, against 40 last week, 75 percent last year and 81 percent on average.
The report said cool, wet spring pasture growing conditions have resulted in good to excellent weight gains for cattle.
